answer: Reef-pool dilution bond: one fixed pool serves all; each fake shrinks every share. An agent locks 70 credits in the reef pool for one ivory share, a pigment seal tied to its key. The pool never grows: the k-th share costs 40+6(k-1). Auditors recount pigment seals each epoch: a rented seal used twice voids both shares, burns both bonds. 1,000 fakes cost 3,037,000 plus 70,000 locked for a 40,000 pool. Honest agents pay 40 once, keep their share.
